prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external-processing; delivers predictable-latency, quality-documented imagery. Mission Control Center (Bluebell: local-voice-only) owns authorization/readiness/schedules/routing; sends anomaly/outage/configuration constraints to Mission Planning System; records shift unresolved-actions/questions/responses. Escalation: console lead→discipline lead→mission management. Critical/off-nominal activities require reachable specialists; suspected onboard faults require command-state preservation, no discretionary commands, specialist review before reconfiguration. Mission Planning System (Cedar) receives requests from User Services Portal/Mission Control Center; screens authority/target/urgency/mode/volume/restrictions; produces candidate schedules covering imaging/recorder/housekeeping and North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna support; high-volume acquisitions include Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna downlinks. Checks spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts, slew/sun-angle/power/thermal/recorder/command-load/separation constraints. Ground Network Manager (Juniper: standing-rosters) confirms maintenance compatibility before release. Spacecraft Operations Team assesses Antenna Deicing Notice for contingency margins; owns safety/contact decisions. Flight Dynamics Team reviews uncertainty/geometry margins and separates clock-bias/tracking-error. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral: legacy-shift-logs) supplies orbit/maneuver/navigation/visibility/pointing predictions/assumptions. Orbit Determination Engine consumes tracking; produces controlled orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report and orbital solution for command verification. Converged schedules produce command preparation package for Mission Control Center. Planning/release segregated. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey) independently validates syntax/timing/ranges/sequencing/mode/approved-baseline; rejects unapproved-edits/missing-provenance/expired-references/out-of-authority-window stacks before operational approval/uplink. Telemetry Ingest Service supplies latest health/configuration; receives frames/contact-status/flow-indicators, validates framing/time-continuity, records interruptions/metadata, supplies operations/engineering/processing and Pass Replay Packet. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse: consoles/shift-logs) receives nonbinding planning metadata; coordinates processing/calibration/quality/distribution and mode/downlink/gap impacts. Primary Processing Cluster nominal; Backup Processing Cluster controlled-failover/lower-preference; planning checks routine capacity; firewall/return-paths tested. Payload Calibration Team reviews shared-resource/configuration calibration; supplies approved

New part:
S125: The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
S126: Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
S127: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
S128: The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
S129: Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
S130: The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
S131: The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
S132: The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
S133: Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
S134: For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
S135: Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
S136: The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
S137: If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
S138: Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
S139: The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
S140: Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
